baseline_reason: Re-baselined for Task 10 (feat/r3f-seoul-day-scene-fill): full day scene-fill landed (Tasks 1-9) plus the Task-10 review fix to the aerial-perspective distant ring. The added static fill (brighter ground bands + denser markings) moved bright_ratio (~0.27->0.59) and marking_ratio (~0.32->0.65) beyond the OLD thresholds; those are baselined here. Task-10 fix: the distant background-ring boxes were LIT (MeshStandardMaterial) so an EXPOSED slab against open sky (e.g. bg-north-west, top-left) read as a hard lit 3D placeholder cube (bright-top/dark-side faces) — a codex-confirmed ship-blocking DEFECT the prior baseline had blessed. Fixed by (a) rendering the day far group UNLIT/flat (MeshBasicMaterial, no per-normal face shading), (b) fog OFF on it (kills the per-fragment depth gradient that re-revealed the box faces), and (c) lifting DISTANT_HAZE_TONE #b9c7d6->#d8e0e5 + DISTANT_HAZE_MIX 0.82->0.87 so an exposed slab washes to the bright UPPER-sky tone it sits against and melts in. Codex before/after: the ship-blocking lit-cube is removed; the residual is a faint flat low-contrast distant-massing silhouette (codex class B, NOT a ship-blocker) — an acceptable stylized real-time world edge. Fully eliminating the residual crisp box silhouette needs real distant-building art/geometry (C-phase visual polish), out of scope for this A-phase re-baseline. Roads codex-PASS (no severed/floating edges). Thresholds in verify-r3f-visual-diff.mjs UNTOUCHED; draw calls unchanged (743/900 peak, 640/650 steady high).
